title: Psychometrics of items: difficulty, discrimination, transfer-predictiveness (item selection and weighting for panels that measure generalisation)
verdict_cn:
结论：可行性中等。"题目怎么挑、怎么加权"有一套几乎不花钱、马上能用的办法；但"按单道题挑出能预测泛化的题"和"直接用生成题做细微比较"目前都做不到，需要先过一道"题目家族"的合格检验。

名词说明：技能文本 = 放进解题模型提示词里的一段说明；父版本 = 当前正在用的技能文本（这里是空骨架）；ids-full = 由五张任务卡组成的初始技能；对照文本 = 和任务无关的安慰剂文字；基准 = 一套考题，如 SearchQA（检索问答）、OfficeQA（办公文档问答）、LiveMath（数学选择题）、SpreadsheetBench（表格编辑）、ALFWorld（文字版家务环境）；cal-1 = 校准实验：SearchQA 的 200 道训练题，11 种文本各答 4 遍，共 8,800 次解题；AUC = 预测准确度，0.5 等于瞎猜，1 为完美；IRT（项目反应理论）= 用少量题推算整卷分数的统计模型；token = 模型计费用的文字单位；置信区间（95% 区间）= 结果在 95% 把握下可能落在的范围。

一、技能文本主要是在"换着题做对"，很少整体提高分数。分数差异里：题目本身难易占 64%，"哪种文本配哪道题"的交叉作用占 12%，文本整体高低只占 1.3%，随机波动占 23%。（我用另写的程序独立重算，数字完全一致。）

二、加分和扣分出在不同的题上，事先大致能看出来。父版本"时对时错"的 52 道题：ids-full 在这里净多对 15 道；父版本"每次都对"的 111 道题：无关对照文本净少对 15 道，v3 候选规则净少对 12 道。用"父版本是否时对时错"预测哪些题会被任务卡改变，AUC 0.85。题目文字本身的特征很弱（最好的一个是"标准答案越短越容易被改善"，AUC 0.64），判题员给的诊断代码没有预测力。

三、IRT 在这里不适用。tinyBenchmarks、metabench 等工作靠 IRT 把题量压到原来的约 1%–3%，前提是"很多模型、单一能力维度、没有交叉作用"。我们这里 72% 的差异来自"文本×题目"交叉作用，复现时 IRT 也没有比随机抽题更好。

四、真正有用的是简单的分层做法：按父版本表现把题分成"总错、时对时错、总对"三层，按层分配题量并按各层在题库里的占比加权。误差降低约 10%，分层抽 60 道约等于随机抽 70 道，而且没有偏差。只有在所有校准文本、约 28 次运行里都做错的题（200 道里 19 道）可以删；"总对"的题绝不能删（删了会让有害文本看起来好 1.3–2.6 分）；不要挑"最容易变的题"（会把 ids-full 的效果高估约 7 分）。

五、要说"对没见过的题也成立"（泛化），题量比重复次数重要。要有 80% 把握测出 5 分的提升，每题答 2 遍，各基准需要约 220–370 道题。按现有题量，能可靠测出的最小泛化效果：SearchQA 6.8 分、LiveMath 8.2 分、SpreadsheetBench 9.1 分、OfficeQA 9.6 分、ALFWorld 12.2 分；过去学到的规则只有 3–5 分，低于所有门槛。

六、生成题目前还不能用于细微比较：在 OfficeQA 上，"有没有技能"这种大差别生成题和真实题一致（相关 0.93），但在"学到的技能对比基础技能"这类小差别上相关为 −0.24，且生成题平均高估约 5 分；SearchQA 的生成题有 67% 每次都做对，几乎测不出东西。

七、"能预测泛化"只能按"题目家族"（同一出题规则产出的一批题）衡量，不能按单题衡量（单题可靠度只有 0.33）。我们定义了家族指标：用约 9 个效果已知的校准文本，看家族的平均变化与真实训练题的平均变化是否同步（相关、斜率、偏差），全程只用训练题、不碰测试集。模拟显示一个完全合格的 100 题家族，95% 的情况相关不低于 0.83、偏差在 ±4 分内，这就是放行门槛。

八、付费小实验 E5-P1（已完成）：先把分析方法写好并封存，再在 180 道从未用过的 SearchQA 训练题上测试（共 1,800 次解题，约 324 万 token，没有一次报错）。
- 泛化得到验证：ids-full 比空骨架高 8.9 分（95% 区间 4.4–13.1 分），和原来 200 道题上的 8.9 分几乎一模一样。
- "伤害出在总对的题上"得到验证：两种有害文本在"预筛两次都对"的题上各掉 16.5–17.7 分。
- 分层抽题仍然有效：误差比随机抽题低约 7%（60 道题的效果约等于随机抽 66 道）。
- 没有验证的一点：只答两遍的预筛里，"时对时错"类太小（只有 9 道），预测不了哪些题会被任务卡改善（AUC 0.51，等于瞎猜）。这次的加分主要出在"预筛两次都错"的题上，所以绝不能凭两遍预筛删题，删掉会丢掉 78% 的加分。各层的细节数字有 20/73 项超出事先给出的范围，说明分层只能用来分配题量和分开读数，不能当成固定预期。
- 实验中途会话中断，后一半晚了约 3.5 小时才做；这段时间服务端没有漂移（前后两次空骨架的分差约 0），前后两半的 ids-full 结果相同。

建议：
- 对目的 1（协同进化）：把验证端要进化的东西定为"出题家族"，先过上面的家族合格检验（每个家族约 2,000 次解题、300–400 万 token），之后每轮把关时顺带更新它的分数；把关时把"有没有加分"和"有没有伤害"分开检验，各看对应的题层。
- 对目的 2（泛化指标）：每个评测基准都报告"对没见过的题"的置信区间，按基准各自分层加权，按上面的门槛决定题量；每题答 2 遍，预算花在更多的题上。
- 预筛（父版本先答两遍）最好和正式测量在同一时段做，或合并多个时段；每轮顺带比较空骨架前后两次的分差，超过约 4 分就重新预筛。两遍预筛只能用来分配题量和单独看伤害，绝不能用来删题。
evidence:
All numbers are measured unless marked.

SearchQA, cal-1: 11 arms x 200 focal training items x 4 runs; 8,785 scored cells of 8,800.

1. **Variance split** (probability scale): item 63.8 %, text 1.3 %, item x text 11.6 %, run noise 23.2 %. SD of text main effects 5.4 points; SD of item x text 15.9 points. The identical-text pair (parent:A vs parent:B) has 0 text and 0 interaction variance. My independent code reproduces every value.

2. **Every text has a reproducible item pattern**, placebos included. Split-half r of item deltas is 0.21-0.73 (ids-full 0.734; 4-run Spearman-Brown 0.85). The null 95th percentile is 0.19-0.24. The same-text null gives -0.25.

3. **Signal-carrying items.** Storey estimates of items changed: ids-full 43.5 of 200; placebos 13.5-46.6; null pair 2.6. ids-full needs 14 items for 50 % of its cross-validated net and 35 for 100 %. control:3's harm is diffuse (21 / 43 / 94 items). 75 of 200 items are constant over all 44 cal-1 runs (25 always-fail, 50 always-pass).

4. **Net effect by parent stratum** (strata from independent sessions; always-fail 37 / mixed 52 / always-pass 111 items):

   | text | always-fail | mixed | always-pass |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | ids-full | +3.5 | +15.1 | -0.9 |
   | control:3 | -0.25 | -5.4 | -15.1 |
   | cand | +3.75 | +2.0 | -12.0 |

5. **Item properties that need no test data.** Targets: 27 task-card responders (ids-full raises the item's pass rate by at least 0.5) and 50 harm-susceptible items.

   | property | AUC |
   |---|---|
   | parent p(1-p) from pooled independent sessions | 0.849 [0.758, 0.927] for responders |
   | parent pass rate | 0.625 [0.55, 0.69] for harm |
   | best item-text feature (gold-answer length) | 0.64 inverted |
   | other text features | about 0.5 |
   | examiner form-code share | 0.39, CI includes 0.5 |

6. **IRT does not fit.**
   - Item x text interaction is 72 % of the excess text deviance (74 % with 16 texts); the interaction deviance is 1,834.7 against a null 95th percentile of 1,037.
   - 9 of 9 residual SVD dimensions exceed parallel-analysis nulls.
   - 2PL slope split-half reliability is 0.41; item-rest correlation reliability is 0.33.

7. **Panel simulation** (RMSE in points, mean over 9 texts, 2,000 panels):
   - At n = 60: random 2.73, Neyman 2.45, p-IRT 2.73.
   - Most-movable selection biases ids-full by +6.96 points.
   - Drop-dead (95 items) biases control:3 by +2.55.
   - Anchor points are biased -2.5 to +2.6 points on texts outside their calibration.

8. **Dead items.** 19 items fail under all 9 texts over a median of 28 independent-session runs; they carry about 0 net. The 75 always-pass-in-calibration items carry harm: control:3 -5.0, cand -2.83 net items.

9. **D-study** (80 % power, 5-point effect, 2 runs per arm). SearchQA ids-full needs 374 items for the population estimand, 122 for the fixed panel, and 251 even with infinite runs. Minimum detectable population effect at the current panel sizes:

   | benchmark (items) | MDE, population | MDE, fixed panel |
   |---|---|---|
   | SearchQA (200) | 6.8 points | 3.9 |
   | LiveMath (100) | 8.2 | 7.3 |
   | SpreadsheetBench (91) | 9.1 | 8.4 |
   | OfficeQA (74) | 9.6 | 7.9 |
   | ALFWorld (57) | 12.2 | 9.1 |

10. **Other benchmarks** (v3 cells, ids-full minus scaffold, points):
    - OfficeQA +7.05 [2.2, 11.9] (74 items);
    - LiveMath -1.84 [-6.2, 2.5] (100);
    - SpreadsheetBench +1.81 [-3.6, 7.2] (91);
    - ALFWorld +9.94 [1.7, 18.1] (57).

    The gain sits in always-fail items on OfficeQA and ALFWorld, but in mixed items on SearchQA.

11. **Generated vs real** (OfficeQA probes).
    - Over 24 contrasts: r = 0.93, generated reads +6.95 points higher.
    - Over the 10 learned-Skill-minus-bzero contrasts: r = -0.24, generated reads +5.28 higher.
    - Selecting generated items by GLM calibration did not reduce the gap: mean |gap| 4.43-5.54 against 4.54 for all items.
    - SearchQA generated panel b06: 112 of 168 items pass every deepseek cell.

12. **TPS_F simulation** (a valid 100-item family, 9 calibration texts, 2,000 draws): TPS_F percentiles 5/50/95 = 0.83/0.93/0.98; slope 0.84; bias 90 % range -4.3 to +4.1 points. With only the 4 small-effect texts, the 5th percentile drops to 0.46.

13. **Pilot E5-P1** (180 fresh items, 1,800 cells, 0 unknown, 0 errors):

    | statistic | pilot | focal expectation |
    |---|---|---|
    | ids-full minus scaffold | +8.89 [4.44, 13.06] | +8.88, z = 0.005 |
    | control:3 | -11.39 | -10.38 |
    | cand | -8.61 [-14.17, -3.06] | -3.12 |
    | always-pass mean, control:3 | -16.5 [-22.6, -11.1] | |
    | always-pass mean, cand | -17.7 [-23.9, -11.7] | |
    | Neyman / random RMSE, n = 60 | 0.926 | 0.94 |
    | AUC, responders by mixed class | 0.514 [0.470, 0.574] | 0.64 (not replicated) |
    | AUC, responders by not-always-pass | 0.751 | |

    - Dropping the 2-run always-fail items removes 78 % of the ids-full gain.
    - 20 of 73 statistics fall outside their focal ranges.
    - Exploratory: no serving drift between the two windows (paired scaffold offsets -0.56 and +0.56 points).
design:
**Item-selection and weighting protocol** (rules R1-R7; free at solver level):
- **R1 (purposes 1 and 2).** Fix the estimand first. A gate and a stage claim are population claims, so use tau-inclusive CIs: an item-cluster bootstrap, or tau-hat from a calibration fixture.
- **R2 (1, 2).** 2 runs per item; spend the rest of the budget on more items. Size panels by the D-study: n = 7.85 (tau^2 + (s_t^2 + s_s^2)/r) / delta^2.
- **R3 (1, 2).** Stratify every focal, regression and similar-target panel on the parent's stratum (always-fail / mixed / always-pass).
  - Allocation: Neyman, proportional to stratum share x calibration SD; weights are the pool shares.
  - Take the gain stratum from pooled multi-run parent cells (train + screen + confirm).
  - A 2-run pre-screen is good only for the not-always-pass split and the harm class.
  - Check the paired scaffold offset each round; re-screen beyond about +-4 points.
- **R4 (1, 2).** Never drop always-pass items (they carry the harm signal). Never select the "most movable" items (that shifts the estimand).
- **R5 (1, 2).** Drop only items dead under a >= 9-text fixture over >= 20 runs (about 10 % on SearchQA). Never drop on a 2-run pre-screen.
- **R6 (1).** Read gain and harm per stratum in the gate (gain: mixed on SearchQA, always-fail on OfficeQA/ALFWorld; harm: always-pass), then combine with population weights.
- **R7 (2).** Strata and weights are benchmark-specific.

**Transfer-predictive properties without test sets.** K calibration texts with known real-pool deltas on a benchmark's TRAINING pool.
- TPS_I (item level) = corr over texts of the item delta vs the pool delta. Reliability 0.33: not usable.
- TPS_F (family level) = corr over texts of the family-mean delta vs the real-pool delta, with slope beta_F and bias alpha_F.
- TPS_X (cross-benchmark) = family delta on benchmark b vs the real training-pool delta on similar benchmark c. It uses the E2/E4/D12 fixtures. Post-hoc evaluation on c's test split stays untouched.

**Generated items** (verification side, purpose 1):
1. **Family validity gate.** About 100 items with guaranteed answers (D6 generator). Run the parent x 2 for strata, plus the 9 cal-1 texts x 1-2 runs. Admit the family if TPS_F >= 0.80 and |alpha_F| <= 4 points. Pre-register these thresholds; a valid family is rejected about 5-10 % of the time.
2. **Steer generation by stratum.** Request items the parent solves sometimes (gain evidence) or always (harm evidence), and reweight to the real pool's stratum shares.
3. **Online validity.** Every gate round appends (family delta, real delta) pairs. Families whose error leaves the bound are demoted. TPS_F and calibration error over the rounds form the verifier's learning curve.
4. **Hierarchical (item-cloning) calibration.** The family mean is the unit of evidence. An admitted family is a measurement instrument, not evidence that a Skill is good.

pilot.result:
E5-P1, pre-registered (plan sha256 00e89672..., analysis code 0344f908...).

Design:
- 180 never-used SearchQA training items: pool 600 minus the 200 focal items, the 60 regression items and the D1-v2 batch.
- Solver deepseek-v4-flash, temperature 0.
- 1,800 cells; 0 unknown; 0 errors.
- Phase A: scaffold x 2 runs. Strata A0/A1/A2 = 41/9/130.
- Phase B: scaffold, ids-full, control:3 and cand x 2 runs.

Results by hypothesis:
- H1 replicated. ids-full minus scaffold +8.89 points [4.44, 13.06] vs focal +8.88 (z = 0.005). control:3 -11.39 (z -0.33). cand -8.61 [-14.17, -3.06] (z -1.51; more harmful than focal -3.12).
- H2 supported. non-A2 minus A2 = +23.7 [10.2, 36.8]. But the gain sits in A0 (+30.5 points, 12.5 of 16 net items), not in A1 (9 items, +5.6).
- H3 supported. Always-pass mean: control:3 -16.5 [-22.6, -11.1], cand -17.7 [-23.9, -11.7].
- H4 fails as registered for cand (-3.89 vs a +-1 criterion). That criterion conflicted with the plan's own focal expectation of -3.25. ids-full: dropping the A0 items removes 6.9 of its 8.9 points (78 %).
- H5 supported. Neyman/random RMSE 0.926 at n = 60.
- H6 first part not replicated. AUC(responders by A1) 0.514 [0.470, 0.574]. Not-A2 gives 0.751; AUC(harm by A2) 0.652.
- H7 not replicated in detail. 20 of 73 statistics fall outside their focal ranges: fresh items are easier (pre-screen 0.747 vs 0.675), and the per-stratum magnitudes shifted.

Deviation: the session interruption put positions 90-180 3.5 h after the pre-screen. Exploratory window split: no drift (paired scaffold offsets -0.56 and +0.56 points), and ids-full is +8.89 in both halves.

Cost: 3,241,924 tokens, equal to the pre-launch median estimate.

risks:
- **Scope.** Most item psychometrics come from one solver (deepseek-v4-flash) on the SearchQA training pool. The pilot covers one benchmark, 4 texts and 180 items.
- **Strata differ by benchmark.** The stratum carrying the gain is mixed items on SearchQA but always-fail items on OfficeQA and ALFWorld. Even on fresh SearchQA items it moved to the 2-run always-fail class.
- **Movability is solver-specific.** It carries over poorly across solvers (r 0.02-0.31), so calibration must use the deployment solver.
- **Rules derived on the same 200 items.** The pilot is the out-of-sample check, and per-stratum details replicated poorly (20 of 73 outside their ranges). Treat strata as allocation and readout tools, not fixed expectations.
- **Serving drift.** One session 16 h earlier showed a +5.75-point offset; the pilot's 3.5-h gap showed none. Pre-screens age unpredictably, so each round needs the paired scaffold-offset check.
- **Few calibration texts.** cal-1 has 9 texts (16 with v3). The family gate (TPS_F) is calibrated only by simulation with real items standing in for a valid family. It has not been tested on a real generated family.
- **Generated-vs-real evidence is old.** It comes from the earlier protocol line (10/15-16 probes, OfficeQA mainly) and has not been redone with coevo5 texts.
- **D-study assumptions.** It assumes binomial run noise and exchangeable items. OfficeQA items share documents, so clustered SEs would raise its n.
- **Pipeline cost tail.** cal-1's ledger charged 26.5M tokens for 8,800 cells against 14.0M delivered: reservations for undelivered calls.
- **Pre-registration flaw.** The H4 criterion was mis-specified relative to the plan's own focal expectation.
- **Interrupted execution.** The pilot ran in two sessions. The killed v1 run's in-flight calls (at most 6) are unrecorded.
cost_estimate:
Spent:
- Retrospective analyses, D-study, simulations: 0 model tokens.
- Pilot E5-P1: 3,241,924 tokens (deepseek only). Mean tokens per cell: scaffold 1,236, ids-full 3,995, control:3 1,254, cand 1,287.

Proposed:
- The panel rules R1-R7 cost nothing extra; the train unit already runs the parent twice per focal item.
- Family validity gate, SearchQA: about 100 x (2 + 9 x 2) = 2,000 cells, about 3-4M tokens per family. With 5 large-effect texts: about 1,200 cells, but small-effect validity would then go untested.
- Online TPS: piggybacks on gate rounds, about 2 x n_F cells per candidate.
- OfficeQA calibration fixture for purpose 2 (74 items x 6 texts x 2 runs = 888 cells): about 4.2-7.0M tokens at the v3 rate of 4,690-7,927 delivered tokens per cell.
- A capped pipeline needs a margin of up to about 2x over delivered tokens (reservations for undelivered calls).
recommendation:
Adopt now (free; purposes 1 and 2):
1. **Declare the estimand of every number.** Report population (tau-inclusive) CIs for gate and stage claims; fixed-panel CIs only for statements about the panel itself.
2. **Use 2 runs per item and buy items, not runs.** A +5-point generalisation claim needs about 220-370 items per benchmark. Current panels detect only 6.8-12.2-point population effects.
3. **Stratify every panel on the parent's stratum** with Neyman allocation and pool-share weights, per benchmark.
   - Take the gain stratum from pooled multi-run parent cells.
   - Use a 2-run pre-screen only for allocation and the always-pass harm readout.
   - Check the paired scaffold offset every round.
4. **Dead items.** Drop only items dead under a >= 9-text fixture over >= 20 runs. Never drop always-pass items or 2-run always-fail items. Never select by movability.
5. **No IRT compression for Skill-text contrasts.** Do not use tinyBenchmarks, metabench, PromptEval or anchor points here; their assumptions are contradicted by the data.

Build next (purpose 1):
6. Make the verifier's evolving artifact a set of generator families behind a pre-registered validity gate: TPS_F >= 0.80 and |alpha_F| <= 4 points at n_F = 100 against the 9 cal-1 texts. First test one SearchQA family (about 2,000 cells, 3-4M tokens), then one OfficeQA family against a 6-text training-pool fixture. Online: update TPS_F every gate round and demote families out of bound. TPS_F and calibration error over rounds are the verifier's learning curve.
7. Steer generation by stratum: generated pools are ceiling-heavy (67 % of the b06 SearchQA items pass every cell).

Purpose 2:
8. Report every target benchmark with the population estimand, per-stratum readouts and benchmark-specific weights. TPS_X may choose evolution-side training items but never replaces the untouched post-hoc evaluation.

Feasibility of this direction: medium. The panel rules are free and confirmed on fresh items. Item-level transfer-predictive selection is not feasible. The family-level gate is feasible but untested on a real generated family.
references:
Verified on arXiv in this session (abstracts; PromptEval and Miller also in the paper body):
- Polo et al., tinyBenchmarks, ICML 2024, arXiv:2402.14992. 100 curated examples for MMLU; the abstract gives no error figure.
- Kipnis et al., metabench, ICLR 2025, arXiv:2407.12844. More than 5,000 LLMs; 28,632 items reduced to under 3 %; RMSE 1.24 % / 0.58 %; one factor, Spearman 0.94.
- Polo et al., PromptEval, NeurIPS 2024, arXiv:2405.17202. 100 templates at about the cost of 2 single-prompt evaluations; the model sigma(f(x_i) - g(z_j)) has no prompt x example interaction.
- Hofmann et al., Fluid Language Model Benchmarking, 2025, arXiv:2509.11106. IRT plus adaptive selection; higher validity and lower variance on MMLU with 50x fewer items.
- Heineman et al., Signal and Noise, 2025, arXiv:2508.13144. No venue on the page; noise = checkpoint variability; filtering noisy subtasks.
- Vivek, Ethayarajh, Yang, Kiela, Anchor Points, EACL 2024, arXiv:2309.08638. 1-30 anchors; 87 model-prompt pairs.
- Madaan et al., Quantifying Variance in Evaluation Benchmarks, 2024, arXiv:2406.10229 (preprint). Item analysis and IRT "struggle to meaningfully reduce variance".
